Three avocado wedges sit on a small paper plate, probably about 7–9 inches across. From the top-down view, the wedges look like roughly a quarter to a third of an avocash each, which suggests about one whole avocado in total.

A medium avocado has about 200 g of flesh. These wedges still have their skin on, and they look a bit browned. Counting the skin, I'd put the total at about 200 g, with edible flesh of roughly 150–170 g. I'll use 160 g of flesh at about 1.6 kcal/g, which gives about 256 kcal.

The question asks for the mass of the food on the plate. I'll report 200 g, since the skin is part of what's there, but base the energy on the flesh, about 250 kcal.
